Rashi on Shabbat 79a:10:1.hebrew: שלשה על שלשה לטומאת מדרס - אבל למגע, שלש על שלש, והן אצבעות:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:10:1.english: Three by three for the impurity of midras - But for [impurity contracted through] contact, [the measure is] three by three, and these are fingerbreadths.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:10:2.hebrew: כך שיעור להוצאת שבת - אלמא שאין מעובד — חמשה טפחים בעינן, ומתניתין מוקי במעובד:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:10:2.english: So too is the measure for carrying out on Shabbat - This implies that for [a hide] that is untanned we require five handbreadths, and our Mishnah is established as referring to [a] tanned [hide].

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:10:3.hebrew: בקורטבלא - מבשלו ברותחין ומתקשה, לישב עליו, ולכסות דלובקאות — שקורין פושדטוויי"ל — ומטות, ולעשותו שולחן:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:10:3.english: In [the case of] a kortovela - One boils it in boiling water and it hardens, [making it suitable] to sit upon, and to cover deluvkaot — which are called faudesteuil [folding chairs] — and beds, and to make it into a table.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:1:1.hebrew: עד שיאמר פרעתי ולא פרעתי - כלומר: עד שלא אמר פרעתי — חייב; משאמר פרעתי — פטור, דבטל ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:1:1.english: Until he says, "I repaid," and "I did not repay" - That is to say: As long as he has not said, "I repaid," [one who carries it out] is liable; once he has said, "I repaid," [he is] exempt, for it has become void for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:2:1.hebrew: דכולי עלמא צריך לקיימו - והכא בפרעו ולא פרעו ממש קאמר, ובשטר מקויים, ודכולי עלמא אסור לשהות שטר פרוע:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:2:1.english: Everyone agrees [that the creditor] must ratify it - And here, [the baraita] is speaking of actual repayment and non-repayment, and [it is dealing] with a ratified [promissory] note, and everyone agrees that it is forbidden to keep a repaid [promissory] note.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:2:2.hebrew: והכא בכותבין שובר קא מיפלגי - יש גורסין: ת"ק סבר אין כותבין שובר על שטר פרוע, שאתה מצריכו לשמור שוברו מן העכברים, אלא מחזיר לו ושורפו, ואסור להשהותו; ורבי יהודה סבר כותבין שובר, ועל ידי שובר מותר לשהות שטר פרוע לצור ע"פ צלוחיתו. ולא היא: חדא, דכיון דאסור לשהות שטר פרוע, אפי' על ידי שובר נמי אסור להשהותו, שמא יאבד השובר וזה חוזר וגובה בו; ועוד, לרבי יהודה "אין כותבין שובר" שמעינן ליה בבבא בתרא (דף קע:), דתנן: מי שפרע מקצת חובו, ר' יהודה אומר יחליף, רבי יוסי אומר יכתוב שובר! וה"ג: ת"ק סבר כותבים שובר. והכי קאמר: משפרעו לוה והוציאו מלוה בשבת — פטור, שאינו צריך לו. ואי אמרת: כיון דראוי לצור ע"פ צלוחיתו, הוא דבעי אהדורי ללוה? לא משהי ליה, שמא יבא לידי מלוה ויחזור ויתבענו; ואי נמי לא מהדר ליה מלוה — לא איכפת ליה ללוה, דמלוה כתב ליה ללוה שובר עילויה. ורבי יהודה סבר: אין כותבין שובר. הלכך, צריך הוא המלוה, דבעי אהדורי, ואי לא מהדר ליה — חוזר ותובעו לו מה שפרעו, דלא סגי ליה בשובר, דצריך לשומרו מן העכברים:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:2:2.english: And here, it is with regard to [whether] one writes a receipt that they disagree - Some have the textual version: The first tanna holds that one does not write a receipt for a repaid promissory note, because you require him to guard his receipt from mice; rather, [the creditor] returns it to him and he burns it, and it is forbidden to keep it. And Rabbi Yehuda holds that one writes a receipt, and by means of a receipt it is permitted to keep a repaid promissory note in order to wrap [it] over the mouth of his flask. And this is not so: First, since it is forbidden to keep a repaid promissory note, even by means of a receipt it is also forbidden to keep it, lest the receipt be lost and this one [the creditor] go back and collect [the debt] with it. And furthermore, with regard to Rabbi Yehuda, we have heard him [say] that "one does not write a receipt" in Bava Batra (170b), where we learned in a mishna: If one repaid part of his debt, Rabbi Yehuda says: He must exchange [the document]; Rabbi Yose says: He writes a receipt! And this is the correct text: "The first tanna holds: One writes a receipt." And this is what [the baraita] is saying: Once the debtor repaid it, and the creditor carried it out on Shabbat, [the creditor] is exempt, as he has no need for it. And if you say: Since it is suitable to wrap over the mouth of a flask, does he [the creditor] need to return it to the debtor [for that use]? [The debtor] would not keep it, lest it come into the creditor's hand and he go back and demand [payment of] it; and even if the creditor does not return it to him, the debtor does not care, because the creditor wrote a receipt for the debtor for it. And Rabbi Yehuda holds: One does not write a receipt. Therefore, the creditor has a need for it, as he must return it [to the debtor], and if he does not return it to him, [the debtor] will go back and demand back from him what he repaid him, since a receipt is not sufficient for him, as he would need to guard it from mice.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:2:3.hebrew: רב אשי אמר - פלוגתייהו כשהוציאו לוה הוא. ומה הוא צריך לו דקאמר? ודאי לא לצור — דמשום סתימת פי צלוחית לא משהי ליה, שמא יבא ליד המלוה — אלא משהי ליה להראותו לשאר בעלי חובות, ולהתהלל שהוא פורע חובותיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:2:3.english: Rav Ashi said: Their dispute is in a case where the debtor carried it out. And what does he need it for, that [Rabbi Yehuda] says [he is liable because he needs it]? Certainly not to wrap [a flask], for [merely] for sealing the mouth of a flask he would not keep it, lest it come into the creditor's hand; rather, he keeps it to show it to other creditors, and to boast that he repays his debts.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:3:1.hebrew: המוציא עור בכמה - משום דבעי למיבעי מיניה הנך בעיי אחרנייתא, בעא מיניה הא, ואף על גב דמתני' היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:3:1.english: One who carries out hide, with how much [is he liable] - Because he wanted to ask him those other questions, he asked him this [one], even though it is [already taught in the] Mishnah.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:3:2.hebrew: לעבד - עור העומד לעבדו, ועדיין לא עבדו — בכמה שיעור הוצאתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:3:2.english: To tan [it] - Hide that is designated to be tanned, and has not yet been tanned — what is the measure of [liability for] carrying it out?

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:4:1.english: One who whitens - [This refers to] wool.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:4:2.english: A sit - The equivalent of the distance between the forefinger and the middle finger.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:4:4.hebrew: אלמא - כיון דמנפץ ומלבן לטווייה קאי, שיעוריה כטוויה:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:4:4.english: Apparently - Since [wool that is] combed and whitened is destined for spinning, its measure is like [that of] spun [wool].

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:4:5.english: Not to tan it - It is not designated to be tanned.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:5:1.hebrew: דוגמא - כלומר מעט, כעין שמראין לדוגמא, לומר: "רוצה אתה בזה?":
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:5:1.english: A sample - That is to say, a small [amount], similar to that which they show as a sample, to say: "Do you want this?"

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:5:2.hebrew: לאירא - והוא כשיעור הצריך לאירא של גרדי, לסתום פי קנה שפקעית הערב נתונה בו:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:5:2.english: For an eira - And that is equivalent to the measure needed for a weaver's eira [plug], to stopper the opening of the reed in which the ball of weft thread is placed.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:5:3.english: Nutshells - The moist peel that is on the shell of the nut.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:5:4.english: Woad - [In Old French:] wesde [woad, a dye-yielding plant].

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:5:6.hebrew: פי סבכה - קופ"א, נותנין בגד באמצעיתה, והאי שיעורא נפיש:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:5:6.english: The opening of a hairnet - *Coife* [a hairnet] — they place a cloth in the middle of it, and this measure is large.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:5:7.hebrew: שאין אדם טורח כו' - ואם בא לשרותה, שורה כדי פי סבכה. אבל עור — טורח אדם לעבד כדי קמיע, ומעובד נמי, פחות מכדי קמיע לא חשיב:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:5:7.english: Because a person does not bother, etc. - And if he comes to soak [dye], he soaks [at least] enough for the opening of a hairnet. But [with] hide, a person bothers to tan [even] enough for an amulet; and [as for] tanned [hide] as well, [anything] less than enough for an amulet is not significant.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:6:2.english: While after one sowed them, we learned - That a single stalk is significant.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:6:4.english: Wasn’t it stated with regard to it - Below, in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Akiva, Rav Pappa resolves it like this:

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:8:1.english: Matza, as per its plain meaning - That it has no processing whatsoever.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:8:2.english: Treated with flour - They leave it in flour and water.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:8:3.hebrew: עפיץ - מתקנין אותו בשחיקת עפצים, כמו שעושין כאן בשחיקת קליפת ארז שקורין טנא:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:8:3.english: Treated with gallnuts - They prepare it with crushed gallnuts, just as they do here with crushed cedar bark, which they call tan [tannin].

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:8:4.english: And how much is its measure - For carrying out on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:8:5.hebrew: רבעא דרבעא דפומבדיתא - רובע ליטרא של פומבדיתא. דרך הסוחרים לצור משקולת של עופרת כדי שלא תפחת, לפי שהמתכת נשחקת תמיד ונפחת מאליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:8:5.english: A quarter of a quarter of Pumbedita - A quarter of a litra of Pumbedita. It is the practice of merchants to wrap a lead weight so that it will not diminish, because the metal constantly wears down and diminishes on its own.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:9:1.english: An amulet - Its measure is smaller than [the amount needed] to wrap a weight.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:9:2.hebrew: לכתוב גט - ותנן (גיטין דף פה.): גופו של גט — ״הרי את מותרת לכל אדם״, ושמו ושמה, והעדים, והזמן. ושיעור זה קטן מכולן:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:9:2.english: To write a bill of divorce - And we learned (Gittin 85a): “The essential [text] of a bill of divorce is: ‘Behold, you are permitted to any man,’” and his name and her name, and the witnesses, and the date. And this measure is the smallest of all of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:9:3.english: And in any case, it was taught, etc. - Evidently, the measure of [hide] that is not tanned is larger.

Rashi on Shabbat 79a:9:4.hebrew: בבישולא - לח, כמו שהופשט. קרי בשולא לשון בשול, שהוא לח, דאכתי לא חזי לעיבוד. אבל יבש חזי לעיבוד, וכיון דחזי לעיבוד — הוי כמעובד:
Rashi on Shabbat 79a:9:4.english: In bishula - Moist, just as it was flayed. [The Gemara] calls [it] bishula, an expression of bishul [cooking], which is moist, as it is not yet fit for tanning. But dry [hide] is fit for tanning, and since it is fit for tanning, it is [treated] as tanned.

Tosafot on Shabbat 79a:2:1.hebrew: ת"ק סבר כותבין שובר - ומיירי שכבר יש לו שובר, ולכך משפרע פטור, דאין זקוק להחזיר השטר. ומתוך פירוש הקונטרס משמע שעדיין לא נכתב השובר; וקשה, דהרי צריך להחזירו ללוה, שלא יצטרך לכתוב שובר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 79a:2:1.english: The first tanna holds: One writes a receipt - And [this] is dealing with [a case where the debtor] already has a receipt, and therefore once he repaid [the debt, the creditor] is exempt, as he is not required to return the document. And from the commentary of Rashi [HaKunteres], it is implied that the receipt has not yet been written; but this is difficult, for surely [the creditor] must return it to the debtor so that he will not need to write a receipt.

Tosafot on Shabbat 79a:2:2.hebrew: חזי דגברא דפרע אנא - כרב אשי תניא בתוספתא דמכילתין: ר' יהודה אומר: אף המוציא שטר פרוע כל שהוא חייב, מפני שמשמרו לבעל חוב. ולשאר אמוראי — קשה לרשב"א:
Tosafot on Shabbat 79a:2:2.english: "Look, I am a man who repays" - In accordance with Rav Ashi, it is taught in the Tosefta of our tractate: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even one who carries out a repaid promissory note of any size is liable, because he preserves it for a creditor. And according to the other Amoraim, [this] was difficult to the Rashba [Rabbi Samson ben Abraham].

Tosafot on Shabbat 79a:4:1.hebrew: אלמא כיון דלטוויה קאי - הוה ליה למינקט: "כיון דלאריגה קאי", שהוא רחוק יותר; אלא שמא לאו כולהו קיימי לאריגה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 79a:4:1.english: "Apparently, since it is designated for spinning" - [The Gemara] should have stated: "Since it is designated for weaving," which is further [along in the process]; rather, perhaps not all [threads] are designated for weaving.

Tosafot on Shabbat 79a:9:1.hebrew: כדי לכתוב עליו את הגט - סבירא ליה כרבי אליעזר, דאמר: עדי מסירה כרתי; דלר' מאיר אין כותבין על הדפתרא, דתנן בגטין (דף כא:): "אין כותבין על נייר מחוק ועל הדפתרא, וחכמים מכשירין", ואמר בגמ': מאן חכמים? ר' אליעזר. ובחנם פי' בקונטרס דשיעור גט קטן מכולן, דהא אשכחן דקלף — כדי לכתוב עליו פרשה קטנה שבתפילין, ונייר, דגרע טפי — שיעורו לכתוב עליו קשר מוכסין; וטעמא — דקלף, שהוא חשוב, אין מצניעין אותו לקשר מוכסין. וכן יש לפרש כאן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 79a:9:1.english: Equivalent to that which is used to write a bill of divorce on it - [The Gemara] holds in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer, who said that the witnesses of transmission effect the severance [of the marriage], for according to Rabbi Meir, one may not write [a bill of divorce] on diftera, as we learned in a mishna in Gittin (21b): "One may not write on erased paper or on diftera, but the Sages validate it." And it was said in the Gemara: Who are the Sages? Rabbi Eliezer. And for naught did the Kuntres [Rashi] explain that the measure of a bill of divorce is smaller than all of them; for behold, we find that [the measure for] parchment is equivalent to [the amount needed] to write upon it the smallest section in tefillin, and paper, which is of even lesser quality, its measure is to write upon it a tax collector's knot [receipt]. And the reason is that parchment, being valuable, one does not save it for a tax collector's knot; and so too can it be explained here.

Tosafot on Shabbat 79a:9:2.hebrew: וקתני מיהא כדי לצור ואמר אביי - קשה לר"י, דלא הוה ליה לאתויי מילתא דאביי הכא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 79a:9:2.english: "And in any case, it was taught: 'Equivalent to that which is used to wrap,' and Abaye said" - The Ri finds this difficult, as [the Gemara] should not have cited Abaye’s statement here.
